Facts in LLMs are often represented as triplets of (subject, relation, object), or (s, r, o) for short. Querying an LLM with a prompt p(s, r), where p expresses the relation r and contains the subject s (e.g., "In which city is the Brandenburg Gate located?"), should result in retrieving the object o (e.g., "Berlin"), provided that the fact (s, r, o) is known to the LLM.
outputs: The object o (a short text answer) for a given subject and relation.
The paper evaluates how well LLMs retrieve factual knowledge before and after in-context knowledge edits, and after applying reversal tokens to counteract malicious edits
